tags.definition: The ego vehicle is on the move along its normal direction of travel during a sustained part of the interval. Do not count an interval whose only ego motion is a turn, lane change, or overtaking maneuver.
The ego vehicle is not moving during a sustained part of the interval.
The ego vehicle turns left, evidenced by a sustained leftward heading change; distinguish this from a lateral lane change.
The ego vehicle turns right, evidenced by a sustained rightward heading change; distinguish this from a lateral lane change.
The ego vehicle moves from its current lane into an adjacent lane on either side without making a road turn.
At least one visible car slows down and its brake lights are illuminated.
At least one visible car is stationary but in a position ready to move; do not count clearly parked inactive cars.
At least one pedestrian is stationary on a pavement and faces toward the road as if waiting to cross.
At least one pedestrian crosses the road, including crossing from either side.
At least one cyclist is visible.
At least one motorcycle or motorcyclist is visible.
A traffic light relevant to the ego vehicle has its red light illuminated.
A traffic light relevant to the ego vehicle has its green light illuminated.

Meaning: The ego vehicle travels in its normal forward direction for a sustained part of the interval; moving and stopped may both occur in different portions of one clip. Required evidence: persistent forward expansion or translation of static road structure across timestamps; changing distance to stationary landmarks or lead traffic that is consistent with ego translation. Temporal test: Confirm forward translation at two or more separated source timestamps, preferably spanning at least 0.5 seconds. Reject when: only another object moves while the static background is unchanged; the apparent displacement is camera shake or a single-frame jump; the only ego action in the interval is a turn, lane change, or overtaking maneuver.

Meaning: The ego vehicle remains stationary for a sustained part of the interval; a clip may contain both moving and stopped phases. Required evidence: static road geometry and stationary landmarks retain nearly the same perspective; the no-translation state persists rather than appearing in one duplicated or blurred frame. Temporal test: Confirm the stationary state at two or more separated source timestamps, preferably spanning at least 0.5 seconds. Reject when: the vehicle is rolling slowly but background perspective continues to change; only the lead vehicle is stationary; motion is obscured by a pan-like turn or transient camera shake.

Meaning: The ego vehicle performs a semantic left turn onto a different road branch or direction, rather than merely drifting left. Required evidence: the continuing road or junction geometry supports a left branch; ego heading changes persistently left from entry to exit and the vehicle aligns with the new direction. Temporal test: Compare pre-turn, turning, and post-turn timestamps when available; require a sustained leftward heading change. Reject when: the vehicle follows a smoothly curving road without selecting a new branch; the vehicle crosses into an adjacent lane while the road direction remains continuous; the apparent turn is caused by camera shake or a moving foreground object.

Meaning: The ego vehicle performs a semantic right turn onto a different road branch or direction, rather than merely drifting right. Required evidence: the continuing road or junction geometry supports a right branch; ego heading changes persistently right from entry to exit and the vehicle aligns with the new direction. Temporal test: Compare pre-turn, turning, and post-turn timestamps when available; require a sustained rightward heading change. Reject when: the vehicle follows a smoothly curving road without selecting a new branch; the vehicle crosses into an adjacent lane while the road direction remains continuous; the apparent turn is caused by camera shake or a moving foreground object.

Meaning: The ego vehicle transfers from its current lane into an adjacent lane while remaining on the same continuing road. Required evidence: a lane boundary or stable lane-relative reference moves across the ego path; the vehicle is first aligned with one lane and later aligned with the adjacent lane. Temporal test: Seek before, boundary-crossing, and after states; require sustained lateral displacement relative to lane geometry. Reject when: the entire road bends while the ego vehicle remains in its lane; the ego vehicle turns onto another road at a junction; overtaking or lateral camera motion occurs without a visible lane transfer.

Meaning: At least one visible car decelerates while that same car's brake lamps are illuminated. Required evidence: track the same car across timestamps; its brake lamps illuminate or become clearly stronger; relative motion, wheel motion, or spacing is consistent with deceleration. Temporal test: Compare the same car before and during braking; do not infer a state transition from one isolated rear view. Reject when: rear lamps are steady tail lamps, reflections, indicators, or glare; the car is already stationary with no observed deceleration; apparent deceleration is explained only by ego motion or a changing camera view.

Meaning: At least one visible car is stationary in traffic or another position from which it appears ready to move. Required evidence: track the same car and verify no meaningful displacement relative to stable road references; its lane or traffic context is consistent with a temporary stop. Temporal test: Confirm stationarity at two or more separated timestamps. Reject when: the car moves slowly but continuously; the vehicle is clearly parked inactive at the kerb or in a parking area; stationarity is inferred from a single frame.

Meaning: At least one pedestrian remains on the pavement or kerb and is oriented or positioned as if intending to enter the road. Required evidence: track the same pedestrian near the road edge across timestamps; the person remains outside the carriageway with body orientation, gaze, or stance directed toward a crossing opportunity. Temporal test: Confirm a persistent waiting state at two or more timestamps rather than a momentary pause. Reject when: the pedestrian is already in the carriageway and crossing; the person walks parallel to the road along the pavement; the person is merely standing near a bus stop, shop, or group without road-directed evidence.

Meaning: At least one pedestrian moves through the carriageway from one side, kerb, or road region toward another. Required evidence: track the same pedestrian across timestamps; the track enters or occupies the road and shows lateral progress through the carriageway. Temporal test: Require displacement across at least two timestamps; use road boundaries and the ego path to establish crossing. Reject when: the pedestrian only waits at the kerb; the person walks parallel to traffic on the pavement; apparent displacement is caused by ego motion while the pedestrian remains stationary.

Meaning: At least one person riding a pedal bicycle is visibly present. Required evidence: a bicycle frame or wheel structure and a rider are jointly visible; the riding posture and vehicle proportions remain consistent across available timestamps. Temporal test: Use multiple views when the object is small or partly occluded; one unambiguous frame is sufficient for presence. Reject when: the two-wheeler is a powered motorcycle or scooter; the object is a pedestrian without a bicycle; a distant silhouette lacks visible bicycle evidence.

Meaning: At least one powered motorcycle, scooter, or its rider is visibly present. Required evidence: the powered two-wheeler body, wheels, and rider geometry are visible; vehicle proportions or bodywork distinguish it from a pedal bicycle. Temporal test: Use multiple views when the object is small or partly occluded; one unambiguous frame is sufficient for presence. Reject when: the vehicle is a pedal bicycle or cyclist; the object is a pedestrian or unrelated narrow vehicle; a distant silhouette lacks powered-motorcycle evidence.

Meaning: A traffic signal governing the ego vehicle's current or imminent path visibly displays red. Required evidence: identify the signal head associated with the ego lane or planned path using lane and junction geometry; directly observe the red lamp illuminated in at least one clear frame. Temporal test: Confirm relevance from surrounding frames when possible; red and green may both occur only if each is clearly seen at different timestamps. Reject when: the signal governs cross traffic, pedestrians, or another lane movement; the red source is a brake lamp, reflection, sign, or lens flare; the colour is inferred from map context or lamp position without visible illumination.

Meaning: A traffic signal governing the ego vehicle's current or imminent path visibly displays green. Required evidence: identify the signal head associated with the ego lane or planned path using lane and junction geometry; directly observe the green lamp illuminated in at least one clear frame. Temporal test: Confirm relevance from surrounding frames when possible; red and green may both occur only if each is clearly seen at different timestamps. Reject when: the signal governs cross traffic, pedestrians, or another lane movement; the green source is a reflection, sign, vegetation, or lens flare; the colour is inferred from map context or lamp position without visible illumination.
